title: Finite immersion cover with sections for a completely decomposed morphism
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Assume that $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and that for every $y\in Y$ there is $x\in X$ with $f(x)=y$ for which the induced map $\kappa(y)\to\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field]. Then there exist an integer $n\geq0$, schemes $Z_1,\ldots,Z_n$, immersions $i_a:Z_a\to Y$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and morphisms $s_a:Z_a\to X$ such that $f\circ s_a=i_a$ for every $a$ and $|Y|=\bigcup_{a=1}^n i_a(|Z_a|)$. In particular, $X\times_Y Z_a\to Z_a$ has the section induced by $(s_a,1_{Z_a})$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The empty target permits $n=0$. No Noetherian, separatedness or quasi-compactness hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0GTL, label lemma-decompose, all four clauses; the section morphisms are the equivalent reformulation used in the proof of Tag 0GTM, label lemma-descend-cd.

proof.text: Fix $y\in Y$. Choose $x\in X$ as in the hypothesis and write $r:\kappa(y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(x)$ for the induced field map. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] there is a canonical $j_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. Set $\sigma=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r^{-1})$. The identity $f\circ j_x=j_y\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] gives $f\circ\sigma=j_y$. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ containing $y$, corresponding to a prime $\mathfrak p$. The open-immersion clause of the latter node and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] identify this pointed map with $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to V\to Y$ and give a $Y$-map $\sigma:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to X$.

source.place: Tag 0GTL, lemma-decompose, proof, first two sentences; Schemes Tags 01J5 and 01HV for the pointed identifications.

proof.text: Use the following small nonempty directed poset: pairs $(I,F)$ where $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$ is a finitely generated ideal and $F\subseteq A\setminus\mathfrak p$ is finite, ordered by inclusion in both coordinates. The upper bound is $(I+J,F\cup G)$, and $(0,\varnothing)$ is a least element. Put $t_F=\prod_{a\in F}a$ and $B_{I,F}=(A/I)_{t_F}$, with the canonical transition maps. Here localization is as in [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. We verify its colimit directly using [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. A cocone of ring maps $B_{I,F}\to C$ is exactly a ring map $h:A\to C$ killing $\mathfrak p$ and sending $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ to units: the stage $((a),\varnothing)$ forces $h(a)=0$ for each $a\in\mathfrak p$, and $(0,\{b\})$ forces $h(b)$ invertible for each $b\notin\mathfrak p$. Conversely these conditions give unique compatible maps from every quotient-localization $B_{I,F}$ by their defining relations. By clauses (c),(d) of [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra], such $h$ corresponds uniquely to a ring map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to C$. This is precisely the colimit universal property, with the canonical maps $B_{I,F}\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

source.place: Tag 0GTL, lemma-decompose, proof, explicit filtered-colimit sentence; Algebra Tag 00CT, proposition-localize-quotient, and the residue-field discussion.

proof.text: Let $Z_{I,F}=\operatorname{Spec}B_{I,F}$ with its structural map $i_{I,F}:Z_{I,F}\to Y$ through $V$. It is an immersion: first the principal open immersion $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)_{t_F}\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ from [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], then the quotient closed immersion from [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion], then the open inclusion $V\to Y$. More explicitly it is a closed immersion into the open $D(t_F)\subseteq V\subseteq Y$, cut out by $I A_{t_F}$; this is the factorization in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. If $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$ then $B_{I,F}=A[T]/(a_1,\ldots,a_m,t_F T-1)$. Thus at every point the affine source $Z_{I,F}$ and affine target open $V$ witness local finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The source is affine, hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and $Y$ is quasi-separated. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] now says $i_{I,F}$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, hence of finite presentation. Finally $t_F\notin\mathfrak p$ and $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$, so the canonical map $B_{I,F}\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ yields a point over $y$.

source.place: Tag 0GTL, lemma-decompose, proof, construction of the immersions; Schemes Tags 01I3, 01IG, 03GI and 01KV; Morphisms Tag 01TP.

proof.text: By Step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit], the inverse system of affine $Y$-schemes $Z_{I,F}$ has limit $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, with its specified map to $Y$. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-limit-lfp-criterion] with $B=Y$, $U=X$, $g=f$ and this small nonempty directed index set. Its surjectivity says the $Y$-map $\sigma$ from Step 1 is represented at a stage: for some $(I,F)$ there is $s:Z_{I,F}\to X$ with $f\circ s=i_{I,F}$, whose restriction to the limit is $\sigma$. Step 3 shows that this stage is an immersion of finite presentation and its image contains $y$. No property of $X$ beyond the assumed local finite presentation of $f$ is required by the cited criterion.

source.place: Tag 0GTL, lemma-decompose, proof, application of Limits Tag 01ZC, proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation, (1) implies (2); Limits Tag 01YW.

proof.text: Choose one resulting pair $(i_y:Z_y\to Y,s_y:Z_y\to X)$ for each $y\in |Y|$. Its images $E_y=i_y(|Z_y|)$ cover $Y$. Each $i_y$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation by Step 3, and $Y$ is qcqs, so [lem-weil-pbc-chevalley-constructible-image] applied to the whole source gives that $E_y$ is constructible. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral] the underlying space of $Y$ is spectral, and [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-clopen-constructible-topology] says every $E_y$ is open in its constructible topology. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-topology-quasi-compact] to this open covering. Choose its finite subcover, enumerate it by $1,\ldots,n$, and retain the corresponding immersions and lifts. They have every required property.

source.place: Tag 0GTL, lemma-decompose, proof, final paragraph; Morphisms Tag 054J, lemma-chevalley; Properties Tag 094L; Topology Tag 0901 and its preceding constructible-topology paragraph.

proof.text: For each retained index $a$, $f\circ s_a=i_a\circ 1_{Z_a}$, so the universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $(s_a,1_{Z_a}):Z_a\to X\times_Y Z_a$. Its composite with the second projection is $1_{Z_a}$, which is exactly a section. If $Y$ is empty, take $n=0$; the union of the empty family is empty and all remaining clauses are vacuous.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NK-77c79d56d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. Its statement matches Stacks 0GTL (more-morphisms.tex, lemma-decompose) clause by clause: completely decomposed is defined inline, f is locally of finite presentation, Y is qcqs, and the conclusions are covering, immersions and finite presentation. The section clause (4) is given in the equivalent form f∘s_a=i_a. The empty case n=0 is correct. The delivery has no new nodes and is not a re-split. Step 1: σ=j_x∘Spec(r^{-1}) satisfies f∘σ=j_y by the naturality node. Passing to Spec κ(p)→V→Y uses the open-immersion clause and j_p=Spec(e^{-1}∘π). Step 2 (elementary): the index of finitely generated I⊆p and finite F⊆A∖p is small and directed, with t_F|t_G for F⊆G. The cocone characterisation is correct, and prime-residue-field-algebra (c),(d) give κ(p) as the colimit. Step 3: (A/I)_{t_F}=A_{t_F}/IA_{t_F} is closed in D(t_F)⊆V⊆Y, the presentation A[T]/(a_i,t_FT−1) is correct, and qcqs-permanence (1) gives finite presentation. Step 4: Spec κ(p) is the limit by 01YW, and the 01ZC criterion (no condition on X) gives a stage lift over Y. Step 5: 054J, 094L, the clopen node and 0901 give a finite subcover, each with its hypotheses checked. Step 6: the section comes from the fibre-product universal property. Edge cases checked: empty Y, a field, a prime that is not finitely generated, and X neither quasi-compact nor separated. Duplicates: only the Noetherian ILO II 2.2.3/2.2.4 nodes come close, and they do not apply to an arbitrary qcqs Y. There is no cycle. I accept the declared tool uses of lem-sfb-scheme-affine-limit-lfp-criterion and the spectral-clopen node.
